solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seasonal visitor Rod repeatedly comes to a Californian location

parts.note: Father Christmas visits once a year, at Christmas
a rod is a bar, and 'repeatedly' says to write it twice
taken as written

explanation.surface: Father Christmas keeps turning up with a fishing rod at some West Coast spot.
explanation.walkthrough: SANTA BARBARA is a coastal city in southern California.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa Barbara is a city on the coast of southern California, so it is a location in that state.

clue.text: Cut not entirely drastic

indicators.note: not the entire word means the last letter is dropped from what follows

parts.note: drastic measures are severe ones

explanation.surface: A reduction that was not quite as harsh as feared.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVERE loses its final E to give SEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever something is to cut it off or through, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Butter with any tang? No, unfortunately

indicators.note: things that go unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up in the wrong order

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A cook complains that the butter has no flavour at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' looks like the dairy spread, but here it means something that butts, as goats famously do.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny goat, like any goat, charges and rams with its head, so it is a creature that butts.

clue.text: Transmit radio broadcast as manager

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered about, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A station boss sends out a radio broadcast in his role as manager.
explanation.definitionFit: An administrator runs an organisation's affairs, which is the job of a manager.

clue.text: Appoint some jackass, ignorant

indicators.note: only some of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone is told to put a stupid, ignorant person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across jackASS IGNorant.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign someone to a role is to appoint them to it, a close synonym.

clue.text: Sacrifice for which Alfred was responsible?

definitions.text: Sacrifice for which Alfred was responsible?

parts.note: surface reading: an offering made to a god, consumed by fire on an altar
setter's reading: King Alfred the Great, in legend, let a peasant woman's cakes burn while he brooded

explanation.walkthrough: The story of Alfred and the cakes is an English schoolroom legend: hiding from the Danes, he was told to watch the baking and let it char.
explanation.definitionFit: A burnt offering is a sacrifice consumed by fire, and Alfred's charred cakes were jokingly just such a thing.

clue.text: My ascending bird — fabulous

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upwards means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Cor!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: An admirer exclaims at a wonderful bird soaring upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cor' is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'My!'. 'Fabulous' here means belonging to fable, not marvellous.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend, so a bird of fable.

clue.text: An academic leader in the mountains

parts.note: taken as written
a dean heads a college or faculty

explanation.surface: A university head is off hiking somewhere up in the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: Andean describes what belongs to or is found in the Andes, the South American mountain chain.

clue.text: Malice of archdeacon, old male

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven
O is the abbreviation for old
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Spiteful feelings from an elderly churchman.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England an archdeacon carries the title 'The Venerable', shortened to Ven.
explanation.definitionFit: Venom in a figurative sense is bitter spite or ill will, which is what malice means.

clue.text: Fighter in crusade in awful scare, a knight

indicators.note: something awful is in a dreadful state, so these letters are left in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A medieval warrior caught up in a terrible fright, along with a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Saracens were the Muslim forces the Crusaders fought, so a Saracen is a combatant in a crusade.

clue.text: Man offering bit of illumination

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a man's first name
second meaning: a narrow beam of light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' stands for any man's name, a common convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray is a man's name, and a ray is a single beam, a small portion of light.

clue.text: Northern personality, note, had to bargain

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for northern
the ego is one's sense of self
ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
to have a meal is to eat it, so had can mean ate

explanation.surface: A northerner of strong character, given a message, was forced to haggle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had to' reads as one phrase meaning 'was obliged to', but 'had' is ATE and 'to' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To negotiate is to discuss terms in search of a deal, which is what bargaining means.

clue.text: A new hint regarding Italian food

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a tip is a useful hint
'as to' means concerning or regarding

explanation.surface: A fresh suggestion about what to eat at an Italian meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the starter course of an Italian meal, cold meats and vegetables served before the pasta.

clue.text: Attempts to provide photographs

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tries, as in having a go
second meaning: pictures taken with a camera

explanation.surface: Someone keeps trying to get some decent pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is both a try at something and an informal word for a photograph.

clue.text: Mark of saint, almost magic somehow?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: done somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put in an unspecified order
almost the whole word means its last letter is left off

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A holy person's sign that might be more or less miraculous.
explanation.walkthrough: Two indicators act on the same word in turn: first trim its tail, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace, and stigmata are the wound marks of Christ borne by saints.

clue.text: Little female and I can go well together

parts.note: F is the short form of female
taken as written
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A small woman and I make a good match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' signals the abbreviation of female, not a small woman. 'Can' looks like a verb, but it is the noun for a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that fit in suit their surroundings and sit comfortably alongside one another.

clue.text: Stars, say, turning up with skimpy attire

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upwards means the preceding word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: e.g. means 'for example', as does 'say'
a mini is a very short skirt

explanation.surface: Celebrities, for instance, arriving in revealing outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' suggests celebrities, which fits the surface of skimpy outfits, but it means a group of stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is a constellation, the Twins, made up of a group of stars.

clue.text: Pray in Bury church with leaders of diocesan evangelism

parts.note: to inter is to bury
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so the opening letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: the initials of these two words

explanation.surface: A churchgoer prays in the town of Bury for diocesan mission efforts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury is a town near Manchester, which is why it has a capital letter here; as a verb it means to inter.
explanation.definitionFit: To intercede is to plead on someone else's behalf, especially by praying to God for them.

clue.text: Girl quiet in the morning

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly
a.m. denotes the morning hours

explanation.surface: A young woman who keeps quiet early in the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam is a girl's name, a short form of Pamela.

clue.text: Artist married one student finally

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for married
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter of the word before is used

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A painter wed one of his pupils in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet was the French Impressionist painter, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: A mister, extraordinary, may be in this group?

definitions.text: A mister, extraordinary, may be in this group?

indicators.note: something extraordinary is out of the ordinary, so the letters are taken out of their normal order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An exceptional gentleman might belong to this elite circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a man who is extraordinary may be counted among the masters of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestri is the Italian plural of maestro, the great conductors and musicians, a select band that an outstanding man could join.

clue.text: Creature not right without head

indicators.note: having no head means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: the side that is not the right is the left

explanation.surface: An animal that is wrong in the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' sounds like mental unsoundness, but it simply means the opposite side.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian, so it is a creature.

clue.text: Playwright's nib's broken around end of line

indicators.note: going around something means enclosing it within
a broken thing is smashed apart, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the word, ignoring the apostrophe

indicators.note: the end of a word means just its last letter is used

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A dramatist's pen has snapped near the end of a line of dialogue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Playwright' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House, so he is an example of a playwright.

clue.text: Beginning job that is on the racecourse

parts.note: beginning and starting are synonyms
a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: A new recruit's first job is at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes rather than names: 'that is on the racecourse' stands for the thing found there.
explanation.definitionFit: The starting post marks where a horse race begins, so it stands on the racecourse.
